LanguageData.DS_AutoIngestDesc: When enabled, the core absorbs loose items across the whole map without requiring hauling (research tier decides 1/5/10 stacks per 15 ticks). Items inside prison cells and workbench ingredient areas are left alone. Stops when unpowered.
LanguageData.DS_CostMultiplierDesc: Range 1/100 to 100x. Build material cost of every building, floor and item; applies as soon as you let go (blueprints already placed keep the price they were placed at).
LanguageData.DS_PowerMultiplierDesc: Range 1/100 to 100x. Electricity consumption of every building; applies as soon as you let go. Generator output is unaffected.
LanguageData.DS_ResearchMultiplierDesc: Range 1/100 to 100x. Research points required for every project; applies as soon as you let go.
LanguageData.DS_EnableDebugLogDesc: Print detailed debug information to the log.
LanguageData.DS_AutoIngestToggleDesc: Allow cores to absorb loose items automatically instead of waiting for a hauler. Turn this off if items seem to teleport around the map.
LanguageData.DS_BackpackMechToggleDesc: Also put the digital storage backpack on colony mechanoids (including drones and robots from other mods). On by default. If you suspect a mechanoid mod is conflicting with this one, turn it off so nothing of ours is attached to mechanoids at all (colonists are unaffected) - a one-click A/B test.
LanguageData.DS_PerfToggleDesc: Fixes four vanilla hot spots that show up when you drag-select or designate a lot, or when a core holds several hundred stacks: selection brackets are culled outside the camera view, designation icons are updated incrementally instead of being fully rebuilt every frame, the "meta puff" fleck burst from mass designating is capped per tick, and a core's existing stock is no longer re-scanned stack by stack every tick by the vanilla haulable lister (the verdicts match vanilla - narrowing the filter still gets it hauled out). Pure performance, no gameplay change. Turn off to fall back to vanilla behavior item by item.
LanguageData.DS_WorkerBudget: Proxy workers: max {0} completions per tick (0 = unlimited)
LanguageData.DS_WorkerBudgetDesc: Each finished job pays a one-time vanilla cost (~0.4-0.5 ms): spawning the drops (which searches for a free nearby cell), spawning the finished building, returning deconstruct materials, spawning harvest yield - each also dirties regions and re-registers things. With 75 parallel workers at 7.5x speed that is 20-40 completions per tick, i.e. 10-20 ms of CPU per tick, while a 60 Hz frame only has 16.7 ms. Lower this to keep frames stable; raise it (or set 0) for raw sweeping speed.
LanguageData.DS_FleckBudget: Max effect flecks per frame: {0} (0 = unlimited)
LanguageData.DS_FleckBudgetDesc: Designating a whole map makes every single designation puff 4-6 "meta puff" flecks - tens of thousands created in one instant, each living 1-2 seconds and drawn every frame, which shows up as "a flash, then a few seconds of stutter". Flecks are purely visual, so anything above the budget is simply not created. Default 500/frame (~30k/sec) is far above normal play.
LanguageData.DS_StorageFilterDesc: Set which item types are allowed into this core. All allowed by default.
LanguageData.DS_BA_ToggleDesc: Turn this off and the crafting proxy stops working recipes for nearby benches (scan range and overclock tier are kept).

LanguageData.DigitalStorage_Letter40_Label: Digital Storage 4.0 - update notes & quick start (2026.10.3)
LanguageData.DigitalStorage_Letter40_Text:
Digital Storage 4.0 — released 2026.10.3

4.0 is a heart transplant: items are no longer numbers in a ledger, they are real Things held inside the core. Apparel, weapons, quality and durability all survive, and vanilla hauling, trading and item scanners recognise them natively.

✅ Existing 3.0 saves are migrated automatically:
- Inventory stored in a 3.0 core (the old ledger) is turned back into real items inside the container; anything that does not fit is dropped at the core's feet instead of being lost.
- Your storage filter is carried over (only the "blocked" side is kept, nothing is loosened).
⚠️ Removed for good: storage interfaces, terminal chips, buffer warehouses and the core upgrade component (capacity now comes from research, see below).
- Interfaces, buffer warehouses, chips and implants that already exist in an old save can no longer be resolved and will disappear when the save is loaded (a few one-off "could not find Def" lines in the log).
Recommended: back up your save before updating.

What changed in 4.0:
- Core capacity starts at 500 stacks and can be researched up to 1000 / 1500 / 3000 (existing cores expand the moment the research finishes)
- Remote access from anywhere at any distance, including cross-map (cores on other maps can supply materials); bill ingredients go straight into a pawn's backpack instead of walking to the core
- Auto-ingest is now a three-tier research path (1/5/10 stacks per 15 ticks), no longer limited by home area or distance
- Proxy buildings (digital workers): 12 dedicated buildings that do the work themselves - mining, construction and deconstruction, cleaning, and growing (sowing, harvesting, tree chopping), in three speed/skill tiers; the Transcendent proxy covers all five work types with up to 75 parallel jobs each
- Crafting proxy: runs the recipes of nearby workbenches on its own, taking materials from the core and delivering products straight back into it, with 3/6/9 GHz overclocking and a vanilla-style "target count" mode
- Caravans, orbital trade beacons and visiting traders can all sell straight from the core
- Compatibility layer: Phinix and its Red Packet plugin are supported, including the "allow trading items that are not in storage" branch

[Crafting proxy - how to get started]
- Build a "Crafting proxy" next to your workbenches. Its range is 13x13; select it and hit the "show range" gizmo to see which benches it covers
- Open the panel: select it and press "Open crafting panel" in the inspect pane, or use the "Craft automation" button on the bottom bar (the top-left of the window switches between crafting proxies on this map)
- Click "Add recipe..." - the list is exactly what the workbenches in range can craft - then click a row to add it to the order list
- Orders have three modes: forever / remaining count / target count (target = pause when satisfied, resume automatically when the products get used up). Type an amount straight into the box, or use -1 / +1 / -10 / +10
- Ingredients come out of a digital storage core and products go straight back into it - the workbench does not need a bill, it only unlocks the recipe
- If it is not working, the detail pane says why: missing material / skill too low / bench unpowered or out of fuel / occupied by a colonist / interaction cell blocked / this bench type cannot be automated
- For more speed, turn on "overclock" in the building's gizmos: 3 / 6 / 9 GHz (speed x3 / x6 / x9 at 9 / 27 / 81 times the power - make sure your grid can take it)
- No power, no work. Tier decides skill (I/II/III/IV = 5/10/15/20); if a recipe needs more, use a higher tier proxy

Thank you for your support! Bug reports: QQ group 693252771.
